contents.html: The Computer Security Division (CSD), a component of the Information Technology Laboratory at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) is responsible for developing standards, guidelines, tests, and metrics for protection of non-national security federal information systems. NIST standards and guidelines are developed in an open and transparent manner that enlists broad industry and academia expertise from around the world. While developed for federal agency use, these resources are voluntarily adopted by other organizations because they are effective and accepted throughout the world. The need for cybersecurity standards and best practices that address interoperability, usability and privacy continues to be critical for the Nation. In Fiscal Year (FY) 2013, CSD continued to align its resources to enable greater development and application of practical, innovative security technologies and methodologies that enhance our ability to address current and future computer and information security challenges. Our foundational research and applied cybersecurity programs continue to advance in many areas including cryptography; identity and access management; cloud, virtualization, and mobile technologies; and advanced security testing and measurement. Strong partnerships with diverse stakeholders are vital to the success of our technical programs. In February 2013, the President issued Executive Order 13636 that directed NIST to work collaboratively with industry to develop a voluntary framework - based on existing standards, guidelines, and practices - to improve critical infrastructure cybersecurity practices. NIST held several workshops, meetings, webinars, and informal sessions to gather feedback with the goals of generating content for the framework and discuss several topics that help inform and guide NIST in this effort. In August 2013, we produced a discussion draft of the preliminary framework. Working closely with standards developing organizations, industry and interagency partners, we are evolving and expanding security automation capabilities to help organizations manage and measure the security of systems and technologies. Our cybersecurity awareness, training, and education programs also exemplify the importance of these partnerships by engaging with academic institutions, federal agencies, small and medium businesses and others to increase awareness and enhance the overall cybersecurity posture of the Nation. Active engagement with the diverse federal community continues to be critical to our success. This interaction is most prominent in our strengthened collaborations with the Department of Defense, the Intelligence Community, and the Committee on National Security Systems to establish a common foundation for information security across the federal government. Through this partnership, NIST released Special Publication (SP) 800-53 Revision 4, Security and Privacy Controls for Federal Information Systems and Organizations, in April 2013.This guideline provides organizations with state-of-the-practice security controls to fundamentally strengthen their systems and the environments in which those systems operate. SP 800-53 Revision 4 and other NIST standards and guidelines contribute to systems that are more resilient in the face of cyber attacks and other threats. Late in FY 2013, news reports about leaked classified documents caused concern from the cryptographic community about the security of NIST cryptographic standards and guidelines. Recognizing community concern regarding some specific standards, we reopened the public comment period for three Special Publications to give the public a second opportunity to view and comment on the documents. contents.html_ja: 米国国立標準技術研究所（NIST）の情報技術研究所に属するコンピュータセキュリティ部門（CSD）は、国家安全保障システム以外の連邦情報システムを保護するための規格、指針、試験、測定基準を策定する責任を担う。NISTの規格と指針は、世界中の産業界および学術界の幅広い専門知識を取り入れ、開かれた透明性の高い方法で策定される。連邦機関向けに開発されるものだが、有効で世界的に受け入れられているため、他の組織にも自主的に採用されている。相互運用性、使いやすさ、プライバシーに対処するサイバーセキュリティ規格およびベストプラクティスの必要性は、引き続き国家にとって重要である。2013会計年度（FY）に、CSDは、現在および将来のコンピューター・情報セキュリティ課題への対応力を高める、実用的で革新的なセキュリティ技術および方法論の開発・応用を促進するため、資源の整合を続けた。基礎研究および応用サイバーセキュリティプログラムは、暗号、識別情報・アクセス管理、クラウド・仮想化・モバイル技術、高度なセキュリティ試験・測定など多くの分野で進展を続けている。多様な利害関係者との強力な連携は、技術プログラムの成功に不可欠である。2013年2月、大統領は大統領令13636号を発令し、重要インフラのサイバーセキュリティ実務を改善するため、既存の規格・指針・実務に基づく自主的な枠組みを業界と協力して策定するようNISTに指示した。NISTは複数のワークショップ、会議、ウェビナー、非公式会合を開催し、枠組みの内容を作成するとともに、この取り組みを導く論点について意見を集めた。2013年8月、予備的枠組みの討議草案を作成した。規格策定団体、産業界、省庁間パートナーと緊密に連携し、組織がシステムおよび技術のセキュリティを管理・測定できるよう、セキュリティ自動化機能を発展・拡張している。サイバーセキュリティの啓発、訓練、教育プログラムも、学術機関、連邦機関、中小企業などと連携して認識を高め、国家全体のサイバーセキュリティ態勢を向上させることで、こうした連携の重要性を示している。多様な連邦コミュニティとの積極的な関与は、引き続き成功に不可欠である。特に、国防総省、情報コミュニティ、国家安全保障システム委員会との連携を強化し、連邦政府全体の情報セキュリティに共通の基盤を確立している。この協力を通じ、NISTは2013年4月に特別刊行物（SP）800-53改訂4「連邦情報システムおよび組織のセキュリティ・プライバシー管理策」を公開した。この指針は、組織がシステムとその運用環境を根本的に強化するため、最新実務水準のセキュリティ管理策を提供する。SP 800-53改訂4およびその他のNIST規格・指針は、サイバー攻撃その他の脅威に対するシステムのレジリエンス向上に寄与する。FY 2013末、機密指定文書の漏えいに関する報道を受け、NISTの暗号規格・指針の安全性について暗号コミュニティに懸念が生じた。特定の規格に関するコミュニティの懸念を認識し、3つの特別刊行物についてパブリックコメント期間を再開し、文書を再確認して意見を提出する機会を国民に再度提供した。この初期措置に続き、2014会計年度には暗号開発プロセスおよびNIST暗号規格・指針の

contents.html: review of our cryptographic development process and NIST cryptographic standards and guidelines in FY 2014. contents.html: Security Testing, Validation, and Measurement Group (STVMG)
contents.html_ja: セキュリティ試験・検証・測定グループ（STVMG）

contents.html: Mission Statement: Advance information security testing, measurement science, and conformance. Overview: Federal agencies,industry,and the public rely on cryptography for the protection of information and communications used in electronic commerce, critical infrastructure, and other application areas. The STVMG supports testing and validation of underlying cryptographic modules and cryptographic algorithms in consideration of established standards. These cryptographic modules and algorithms enable products and systems to provide security services, such as confidentiality, integrity, and authentication. Although cryptography provides security, poor designs or weak algorithms can render a product insecure and place highly sensitive information at risk. When protecting sensitive data, Federal Government agencies require a minimum level of assurance that cryptographic products meet established security requirements and use only tested and validated cryptographic modules. STVMG’s testing-focused activities include validating cryptographic algorithm implementations, cryptographic modules, and Security Content Automation Protocol (SCAP)-compliant products; developing test suites and test methods; providing implementation guidance and technical support to industry forums; and conducting education, training, and outreach programs.
contents.html_ja: 使命：情報セキュリティの試験、測定科学および適合性を推進する。概要：連邦機関、産業界および一般市民は、電子商取引、重要インフラその他の分野で用いる情報と通信を保護するため暗号技術に依存している。STVMGは、確立済み標準に照らして基礎となる暗号モジュールおよび暗号アルゴリズムの試験・検証を支援する。これらのモジュールとアルゴリズムにより、製品およびシステムは機密性、完全性、認証などのセキュリティサービスを提供できる。暗号技術はセキュリティを提供する一方、設計不良や脆弱なアルゴリズムは製品を安全でなくし、極めて機微な情報を危険にさらし得る。機微情報を保護する連邦政府機関は、暗号製品が確立済みセキュリティ要件を満たし、試験・検証済みの暗号モジュールのみを使用しているという最低限の保証を必要とする。STVMGの試験中心の活動には、暗号アルゴリズム実装、暗号モジュールおよびSCAP準拠製品の検証、試験スイートと試験方法の開発、業界フォーラムへの実装指針・技術支援、教育・研修・アウトリーチプログラムが含まれる。

This Executive Order directed NIST to work with stakeholders to develop a voluntary framework – based on existing standards, guidelines, and practices − for reducing cybersecurity risks to critical infrastructure. The NNLT worked with the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) on the OPM Cross-Agency Priority Goal: “Closing Skills Gap” for IT/Cybersecurity and on the OPM Special CybersecurityWorkforce Project focused on reducing cybersecurity workforce skills gaps. The project will allow agencies to identify and address their needs for cybersecurity skill sets to meet their missions. In accomplishing this project, agencies will also be updating their cybersecurity positions with codes that revise the definitions of and taxonomy used for cybersecurity work. In FY 2013, the NNLT supported DHS in the launch of the National Initiative for Cybersecurity Careers and Studies (NICCS), (http://niccs.us-cert.gov), an online resource for cybersecurity career, education, and training information. Additionally, CSD expanded the dissemination of its publications to the Association for Computing Machinery (ACM) Digital Library (DL). ACM DL now has a “collection” of NIST Computer Security Publications, which includes SP 800-series publications. CSD initiated an internal project to test the feasibility of creating electronic book (e-book) editions of its FIPS, SPs and NISTIRs, to supplement the PDF editions currently available on CSRC. contents.html: policies are correctly specified. Incorrect AC policies result in faults that not only leak but also disable access to information, and faults are especially difficult to detect without support of formal embedded models such as Multi-Level Security (MLS) and Chinese Wall. Most research on AC model or policy verification techniques are focused on one particular model, and almost all of the research is in applied methods, which require the completed AC policies as the input for verification or test processes to generate fault reports. Even though correct verification is achieved and counterexamples may be generated along with found faults, those methods provide no information about the source of rule faults that might allow conflicts in privilege assignment, leakage of privileges, or conflict of interest permissions. The difficulty in finding the source of faults is increased especially when the AC rules are intricately covering duplicated variables to a degree of complexity. Languages

Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE)A nomenclature and dictionary of security-related software flaws

contents.html: NIST released draft NISTIR 7946, CVSS Implementation Guidance, which guides analysts scoring IT vulnerabilities using the CVSS Version 2.0.That document is the result of applying the CVSS specification to score over 50,000 vulnerabilities analyzed by the NVD. The report reviews the CVSS base metrics and provides guidance for difficult and/or unique scoring situations and assists vulnerability analysts with scoring particular types of vulnerabilities by identifying common keywords and phrases that often appear in vulnerability alerts. The report includes a collection of scored IT vulnerabilities from the NVD, a justification for each score provided, and a description of the NVD vulnerability scoring process. NIST, in collaboration with industry partners in the IETF, established the Security Automation and Continuous Monitoring (SACM) working group, chartered in July 2013. The current scope of work for SACM includes identifying and/or defining the transport protocols and data formats needed to support the collection and evaluation of device state against expected values and standards for interacting with repositories of security automation content.The initial focus of the SACM working group is on identifying use cases, requirements, and architectural
contents.html_ja:
NISTはCVSS実装ガイダンスであるNISTIR 7946草案を公開した。これはCVSSバージョン2.0を使い、IT脆弱性にスコアを付ける分析者を支援する。NVDが分析した5万件を超える脆弱性にCVSS仕様を適用した結果に基づく。レポートはCVSS基本評価指標を解説し、難しい事例や特異な事例の採点指針を示す。また、脆弱性警告によく現れる語句を特定し、特定の種類の脆弱性を採点する分析者を支援する。NVDから採点済み脆弱性を収録し、各スコアの根拠とNVDの採点プロセスを説明する。

If the implementer deviates from or excludes any Algorithm/Component part of these instructions or requirements, the validation test will fail, indicating that the algorithm implementation does not Standard (TDES) function properly or is incomplete. CAVP-developed validation tests are performed by accredited testing laboratories on a vendor’s algorithm implementation using automated known-answer tests, which compare the result from a cryptographic operation with a specific input against the expected result. They provide a uniform way to assure that the cryptographic algorithm implementation adheres to the detailed specifications. There are several types of validation tests, all designed to satisfy the testing requirements of the cryptographic algorithms and their specifications. These include, but are not Elliptic Curve limited to, Known-Answer Tests, Monte Carlo Tests, and Multi- Digital Signature Block Message Tests. The Known-Answer Tests are designed Algorithm (ECDSA) October 5, 2001 andANSI X9.62 to examine the individual components of the algorithm by supplying known values to the variables and verifying the expected result. The Monte Carlo Test is designed to exercise RSA algorithm the entire IUT. This test is designed to detect the presence of implementation flaws that are not detected with the controlled input of the Known-Answer Tests. The types of implementation flaws detected by this validation test include pointer problems, insufficient allocation of space, improper error handling, and incorrect behavior of the IUT. The Multi-Block Message Test (MMT) is designed to test the ability of the implementation to process multi-block messages, which require the chaining of information from one block to the next. During the last few years, CSD has expanded its publications 512/224, SHA-512/256 beyond only an algorithm’s specification into how an algorithm Random number should be used. Many of these requirements are outside the generator (RNG) scope of the algorithm boundary and therefore cannot be tested algorithms at the algorithm level by the CAVP. contents.html_ja: これらの指示または要件に含まれるアルゴリズム／コンポーネントのいずれかから逸脱したり、それを除外したりすると、検証試験は失敗し、アルゴリズム実装が正常に機能していないか不完全であることを示す。CAVPが開発した検証試験は、認定試験機関がベンダーのアルゴリズム実装に対して実施する。自動Known-Answer Testでは、暗号演算に特定の入力を与えた結果を期待値と比較する。これらの試験は、暗号アルゴリズム実装が詳細仕様に準拠していることを確認するための統一的な方法を提供する。検証試験には複数の種類があり、いずれも暗号アルゴリズムおよびその仕様の試験要件を満たすよう設計されている。これにはKnown-Answer Test、Monte Carlo Test、Multi-Block Message Testなどが含まれるが、これらに限定されない。Known-Answer Testは、変数に既知の値を与えて期待値を検証することにより、アルゴリズムの個々の構成要素を調べる。Monte Carlo TestはIUT全体を実行し、制御された入力を用いるKnown-Answer Testでは検出できない実装上の欠陥を検出するよう設計されている。この検証試験で検出する欠陥には、ポインターの問題、メモリ領域の割り当て不足、不適切なエラー処理、IUTの誤った動作が含まれる。Multi-Block Message Test（MMT）は、複数ブロックのメッセージを処理する実装能力を試験する。複数ブロックの処理には、あるブロックから次のブロックへ情報を連鎖させる必要がある。ここ数年、CSDはアルゴリズム仕様だけでなく、アルゴリズムの使用方法も扱う出版物を拡充してきた。こうした要件の多くはアルゴリズムの境界範囲外であり、CAVPはアルゴリズムレベルで試験できない。要件の一部はCMVPの範囲内だが、CAVPとCMVPのどちらの範囲にも含まれないものもある。要件が両者の範囲外にある場合、それを使用する、インストールする、または設定するアプリケーションやプロトコルの主体が要件を満たす責任を負う。例えば、暗号モジュールの設計によっては、特定の鍵が複数の目的に使われているかをモジュールが判定できない場合がある。これは強く推奨されない状況である。

contents.html: components, must be trustworthy. A vulnerability in any of those components could compromise the trustworthiness of the security mechanisms that rely upon those components. Stronger security assurances may be possible by grounding security mechanisms in roots of trust. Roots of trust are highly reliable hardware, firmware, and software components that perform specific, critical security functions. Because roots of trust are inherently trusted, they must be secure by design. As such, many roots of trust are implemented in hardware so that malware cannot tamper with the functions they provide. Roots of trust provide a firm foundation from which to build security and trust. A focus area for CSD’s roots of trust research in FY 2013 was security for mobile devices. contents.html: Josh Franklin and Kelley Dempsey won the (ISC)² Government Information Security Leadership Award (GISLA) in the Process/ Policy Improvement category for their work on the Federal Mobile Security Baseline and the Mobile Computing Decision Framework. According to (ISC)², the award in this category is given to “An individual or team of senior-level U.S. federal government personnel…whose contribution to the development or implementation of any information security policy or process has significantly improved the security posture of a federal agency, department or government-wide within the last 12 months.” Source: https://www.isc2.org/gisla/Default.aspx.
contents.html_ja: Josh Franklin氏とKelley Dempsey氏は、Federal Mobile Security BaselineおよびMobile Computing Decision Frameworkに関する取り組みにより、Process/Policy Improvement（プロセス／ポリシー改善）部門で(ISC)² Government Information Security Leadership Award (GISLA)を受賞した。(ISC)²によると、この部門の賞は「過去12か月以内に、情報セキュリティポリシーまたはプロセスの策定もしくは実施への貢献によって、連邦機関、部門、または政府全体のセキュリティ態勢を大幅に改善した米国連邦政府の上級職員である個人またはチーム」に授与される。出典：https://www.isc2.org/gisla/Default.aspx.

contents.html: Dr. Ron Ross Inaugural Lynn F. McNulty Information Security Leadership Tribute Award National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Fellow Ron Ross has been awarded the inaugural Lynn F. McNulty Tribute U.S. Government Information Security Leadership Award. The (ISC)2 U.S. Government Advisory Board for Cyber Security (GABCS) announced the award on October 29, 2013, in recognition of Ross’s “key role in establishing cybersecurity requirements for federal agencies for decades.” The award was established last year after the death of (ISC)2 Fellow and IT security evangelist Lynn F. McNulty, CISSP. McNulty was considered by those in the community as the “pioneer” of government information security. The Tribute Award recognizes a member of the U.S. federal information security community who upholds McNulty’s legacy as a visionary and innovator through outstanding service and commitment. Ross worked with McNulty during the 1990s when McNulty was NIST’s Associate Director of Computer Security. “Ron’s insight and leadership in producing a library of guidance publications over the past decade has greatly contributed to the advancement of information security in government and around the world,” said Peter Gouldmann, CISSP, director of information risk programs, Office of Information Assurance, U.S. Department of State, and member, (ISC)2 GABCS. “His highly collaborative approach, incorporating government and industry, has resulted in products that are being adopted and adapted for use on national security systems, transcending the unclassified and classified systems landscape.” Sources: https://www.isc2.org/GISLA-Lynn-McNulty-Award/defalt.aspx http://www.nist.gov/itl/csd/ross-110513.cfm
contents.html_ja: Ron Ross博士　Inaugural Lynn F. McNulty Information Security Leadership Tribute Award（第1回Lynn F. McNulty情報セキュリティ・リーダーシップ功労賞）。National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)フェローのRon Ross氏が、第1回Lynn F. McNulty Tribute U.S. Government Information Security Leadership Awardを受賞した。(ISC)2 U.S. Government Advisory Board for Cyber Security (GABCS)は、連邦機関のサイバーセキュリティ要件を数十年にわたり確立するうえでRoss氏が「重要な役割」を果たしたことをたたえ、2013年10月29日に受賞を発表した。この賞は、(ISC)2フェローでITセキュリティの普及に尽力したLynn F. McNulty氏（CISSP）の死去を受け、前年に創設された。McNulty氏はコミュニティで政府情報セキュリティの「先駆者」とみなされていた。この功労賞は、優れた奉仕と献身を通じ、先見性と革新性を備えたMcNulty氏の遺産を受け継ぐ米国連邦情報セキュリティコミュニティのメンバーを表彰する。Ross氏は、McNulty氏がNISTのコンピュータセキュリティ担当副所長だった1990年代に同氏と共に働いた。(ISC)2 GABCSのメンバーである、米国国務省情報保証局の情報リスクプログラム責任者Peter Gouldmann氏（CISSP）は次のように述べた。「過去10年間にわたりガイダンス文書群を作成したRon氏の洞察力とリーダーシップは、政府および世界各地の情報セキュリティの進展に大きく貢献した。政府と産業界を取り込む高度に協調的なアプローチによって、機密区分の有無を超えて国家安全保障システムに採用・適用される製品が生み出された。」出典：https://www.isc2.org/GISLA-Lynn-McNulty-Award/defalt.aspx http://www.nist.gov/itl/csd/ross-110513.cfm。

contents.html: The Computer Security Division uses multiple NIST Technical Series to promulgate security standards, guidelines, recommendations, research, and additional background material. Those series include Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS), NIST Special Publications (SPs), NIST Interagency or Internal Reports (NISTIRs) and Information Technology Laboratory (ITL) Bulletins. Links to these publications are available at http://csrc.nist.gov/publications. Additionally, each year CSD staff authors numerous additional publications, including journal articles, conference papers, and other papers that are widely disseminated. They range from basic research to high-level summaries of CSD activities.
contents.html_ja: Computer Security Division（CSD）は、セキュリティ標準、ガイドライン、推奨事項、研究、およびその他の背景資料を発行するため、複数のNIST Technical Seriesを利用する。これらのシリーズには、Federal Information Processing Standards (FIPS)、NIST Special Publications (SP)、NIST InteragencyまたはInternal Reports (NISTIR)、およびInformation Technology Laboratory (ITL) Bulletinsが含まれる。これらの刊行物へのリンクはhttp://csrc.nist.gov/publications. これらは入手できる。さらに、毎年CSD職員は、広く普及する学術誌論文、会議論文、その他の論文を多数執筆する。それらは基礎研究からCSD活動の概要まで多岐にわたる。

contents.html: NIST Cloud Computing Public Security Working Group [M. Iorga], “Challenging Security Requirements for US Government Cloud Computing Adoption,” National Institute of Standards and Technology, Gaithersburg, Maryland, November 27, 2012, 61 pp. The Federal Cloud Strategy, February 8, 2010, outlines a federal cloud computing program that identifies program objectives aimed at accelerating the adoption of cloud computing across the Federal Government. NIST, along with other agencies, was tasked with a key role and specific activities in support of that effort, including the delivery of the NIST Cloud Computing Technology Roadmap and the publication of other Special Publications that address the reference architecture, definitions, and security aspects of cloud computing. In order to achieve adoption of cloud computing for the Federal Government, it is necessary to address the security and privacy concerns that federal agencies have when migrating their services to a cloud environment. To further exacerbate the situation, there are few documented details that directly address how to achieve some security aspects in a cloud environment. The purpose of this document is to provide an overview of the high-priority security and privacy challenges perceived by federal agencies as impediments to the adoption of cloud computing. The document provides descriptions of the existing mitigations to these security and privacy impediments. If no mitigations are listed, then ongoing efforts that could lead to mitigations are described. In the cases where no ongoing efforts were identified,the document makes recommendations for possible mitigation or references existing best practices.
